stt: Ask HN: Mind bending books to read and never be the same as before?
x:
I really enjoy books on neuroscience that change the way I think about perception.

Phantoms in the Brain by V S Ramachandran - a book about how the brain organises itself in bizarre edge cases. The Tell-Tale Brain: A Neuroscientist's Quest for What Makes us Human. The Tell-Tale Brain: A Neuroscientist's Quest for What Makes us Human by the same author is also worth reading.

Admissions by Henry Marsh - An experienced neurosurgeon's account of how his job has changed over the decades. Really interesting discussion of what's important and how people react in a real crisis.

The Man Who Mistook His Wife For A Hat by Oliver Sacks. More of a collection of interesting curiousities but does an amazing job of humanising the discussion of brain.

stt: Ask HN: Which book can attract anyone towards your field of study?
x:
What a great question!

The book that got me into neuroscience was Phantoms in the Brain by V. S Ramachandran and Sandra Blakeslee. A 22-year old book that wowed 20-year-old me.  Principles of Neural Design by Peter Sterling and Simon Laughlin is a more recent book. It is brilliant, beautifully written and probably should be required reading for anyone looking to do graduate studies in neuroscience. In a field inundated with data and siloes and jargon, it bats for a focus on jargon-free understanding of principles that can explain much of the complexity. It was hugely inspirational for us when doing our own book (plug alert!).

I hope that Journey of the Mind: How Thinking Emerged from Chaos, a book I co-authored, a book which drew inspiration from these two books, is able to do the same for many looking to study neuroscience and AI now.

Phantoms in the Brain https://www.amazon.com/Phantoms-Brain-Probing-Mysteries-Huma...

Principles of Neural Design https://www.amazon.com/Principles-Neural-Design-MIT-Press/dp...

Journey of the Mind https://www.amazon.com/Journey-Mind-Thinking-Emerged-Chaos/d...

For compelling examples of the brain seemingly deliberate activities that occur  without humans conscious awareness, highly recommend the great examples in:

"Phantoms in the Brain": https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/31555.Phantoms_in_the_Br...
